_note: Source of truth for Claude Code's /model and /effort pickers. Hand-maintained because CC does not expose available models programmatically (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/12612). Updates: use the `update-lucidos-cc-models` skill, which diffs this file against `claude /model` and bumps entries to match. include_str!() baked at compile time, parsed once via LazyLock, so there is no runtime IO cost. At most ONE entry may claim top capability: Fable 5 is the tier above Opus, so an Opus entry must not be described as 'most capable'. That contradiction shipped once (Opus 5 vs Fable 5) and is easy to reintroduce when a new model is added. An alias row (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`) is labelled version-free on purpose: CC repoints those aliases over time, so naming a version there goes stale silently. Pin a full model id for anything the picker recommends. There is deliberately no `sonnet[1m]` / `claude-sonnet-5[1m]` row: CC documents `sonnet[1m]` as having no effect once `sonnet` resolves to Sonnet 5, which has a native 1M window, so a row that selects nothing different is drift. The historical label for `sonnet[1m]` is kept in the frontend's STATIC_MODEL_LABELS so older threads still render it.
